value.label: MECHANISM BEHIND rho — NAMED AND MEASURED
value.pin: 70 — name the mechanism; a measured rho is a number, a mechanism is a model
value.answer_to_the_pins_first_question: YES — CONFIRMED, both structurally and empirically

structural_finding.obs_channel: eps = obs_noise(i, obs_identity, r, root) — keyed on OBSERVATION identity (_obs_identity(lon, lat, t, mission))
structural_finding.element_channel: eta_t = coef_noise(i, els_identity, q, root) — keyed on ELEMENT identity
structural_finding.root: BOTH seam tiles run at the SAME root (scripts/phase14_stage1_run.py: tiles[tile] = _seam_tile_leg(tile, m=m, maxiter=maxiter, root=root))
structural_finding.therefore: the two tiles' strip observation sets are IDENTICAL (Jaccard 1.0000) and the root is shared, so the eps' draws for those observations are the SAME REALISATIONS. The eta~ draws are independent because the pavements share ZERO element centres. The obs-perturbation channel is ALREADY PAIRED; only the element channel is independent.

empirical_test.design: a shared DRAW is member-aligned; a shared FIELD is not. So member k of seam_n should correlate with member k of seam_s, while member j vs member k (j != k) should not. Measured on the strip from the persisted member stores, members centred on the member mean.

the_model_pin_70a.relation: rho_sigma ~ r^2, where r is the matched-member FIELD correlation between the two tiles on the evaluation domain
the_model_pin_70a.agreement: model 0.0637 vs implied 0.0517 — same magnitude, ~23% apart, from a model with NO fitted parameter
the_model_pin_70a.why_this_is_a_model_not_a_number: r is a function of how much of the member variance rides the SHARED obs channel versus the independent element channel. That fraction scales with the shared-observation fraction on the evaluation domain and with obs density — which is exactly the parameterisation pin 45(c) needs. rho for one pair is a number; rho = r^2 with r measurable per pair is a model.

sharpened_t14_prediction_pin_70b.formula: T_cross ~ E[T](m) * sqrt(1 - r^2), with r MEASURED on the strip after the change
sharpened_t14_prediction_pin_70b.after_t14: T14 pairs the ELEMENT channel too, so r RISES toward the fraction of the member field explained by common draws. The fall in T_cross therefore has a MAGNITUDE, not merely a direction: re-measure r on the strip and predict T_cross from it BEFORE reading the sigma rows. If r reaches ~0.9, T_cross ~ 0.44; if the element channel pairs only partially, r and T_cross move together and the formula still holds.
sharpened_t14_prediction_pin_70b.how_to_falsify: measure r after T14 and compare the predicted T_cross to the observed one. If they diverge, the r^2 model is wrong and the floor cannot be parameterized by it. This is a sharper test than the direction-only prediction of pin 68(b), and it SUPERSEDES nothing there — the direction prediction stands, this adds the magnitude.

value.headline: On the EVALUATION STRIP the two tiles' observation sets are IDENTICAL: 14,876 observations each, 14,876 shared, Jaccard 1.0000. does_it_account_for_the_deficit.derivation: Var(sigma_a - sigma_b) = 2 sigma^2 (1-c4^2)(1-rho), so T scales as sqrt(1-rho); rho = 1 - (T_cross/E[T])^2
does_it_account_for_the_deficit.verdict: YES. A correlation of only ~5% between the two sigma fields' sampling errors accounts for the ENTIRE 4.2 sd deficit. That magnitude is consistent with identical observations combined with INDEPENDENT draws: the draws contribute no correlation, but the identical data geometry does.

value.consequence_for_rule_0b_pin_68a: Rule 0.b's independence premise was NEVER correct for the pair route, ON ANY LATTICE. C_control_seam_s_vs_anchor_same_origin.reading: seam_s and the seamless anchor share (x0, y0) = (0, 0), so the same physical element carries the same identity and the IDENTICAL draw — which is exactly why RMS(sigma_s - sigma_anchor) nearly vanishes while RMS(sigma_n - sigma_anchor) sits at the MC floor

confirmed: MAGNITUDE — RMS(sigma_n - sigma_s) = 0.003607 m matches the two-independent-estimate MC floor sigma/sqrt(m-1) = 0.003708 m to 2.7%

ONE-SIDEDNESS — the disagreement against the seamless anchor is carried almost entirely by seam_n; seam_s, which shares the anchor's basis origin and therefore its CRN draws, nearly vanishes against it. A seam artifact would be symmetric in the two tiles
NO LOCALISATION — the sigma difference is flat across the strip, while the mean route on the same strip shows the expected V with its minimum at the shared core boundary

HALF-SPLIT — within-tile 50/50 member halves, which cross no seam at all, disagree MORE than the two tiles do, at the sigma/sqrt(49) floor. This is the discriminating result: a seam artifact cannot appear inside a single tile

refuted: The reading that PAIR/sigma ELEVATED is a SEAM artifact — a cross-tile disagreement caused by the tiling — is not supported: the same magnitude arises inside one tile with no seam present, it does not localise at the boundary, and it is one-sided in a way a seam cannot be

Measured peak is 4365 MiB, so the 2x launch rule needs ~8730 MiB — and live headroom was observed at 11,248 MiB on this box during this very run. RAM is achievable at the top of the co-tenant cycle.
